en: Run the money side of a construction company in one workbook
Profit, overheads, order book and cash in one place
Monthly profit and loss that builds itself
revenue, direct cost, overheads, depreciation, tax and net profit for each month come from your project and overhead sheets
WIP report with over and under billing
cost to date gives the share complete and the revenue earned, then compares it with what you billed and flags projects out of balance
every project is ranked by profit and by margin and compared with the margin at tender, so a fading job shows at once
eight overhead groups each month with the variance, the share of the month and a flag when a line runs over
Order book and backlog in months of work
work won, work built and the backlog at each month end, with the months of work secured against the months you want
value times chance gives the work you can count on and the profit you expect, with a warning when a decision is late
current and quick ratio, days sales outstanding, days purchases outstanding and rolling margins show cash trouble before it arrives
Loans with the payment worked out
payment, payments made, balance, end date and interest over the life for every loan and lease
cost, life and residual value give the charge each year, the book value and a flag for assets near the end of their life
days left and a warning before every policy renewal, tax return and licence, with the amount due
the true cost of each staff member and each vehicle, the part projects recover and the cost per hour and per km
revenue and margin targets compared with the actual figures from the project sheets and the share achieved

Projects with contract value, revenue and cost to date
One row for each project with its client, manager, contract value and dates; months, revenue, cost, share done and retention held fill in from Revenue by Month.
Revenue recognised by month and project
One row for each project and month with the revenue earned and the direct cost; gross profit, margin and retention held fill in.
Work in progress: earned revenue against billing
One row for each project with its estimated cost, billing to date and review date; cost to date, share complete, earned revenue, over or under billing and the profit fade fill in.
One row for each project with its margin at tender; revenue, cost, gross profit, margin, fade from the tender margin and the rank by profit and by margin fill in.
Order book: secured work still to build
One row for each contract still running with the margin you expect on what is left; revenue to date, work remaining, months left, monthly burn, remaining profit and share of the book fill in.
Backlog by month: work won, built and left
One row for each month with the contracts you won and any change; revenue built, opening and closing backlog, months of work and cover for new work fill in.
Tender pipeline value and expected profit
One row for each opportunity with its value, chance and expected decision; weighted value, expected profit, days to decision and a status fill in.
One row for each month with other income and interest paid; revenue, direct cost, overheads, depreciation, tax, net profit and margins fill in from the other sheets.
Budget for the year against actual
One row for each month with your budget for revenue, direct cost and overheads; budget profit, actual revenue and profit, the variances and a status fill in.
Key ratios by month: liquidity, collection and margins
One row for each month with cash, receivables, stock, payables and short term debt; the current and quick ratios, days of sales and purchases outstanding and rolling three month margins fill in.
One row for each month and overhead group with budget and actual; the variance, its share, the share of the month and a status fill in.
Staff costs: salary, on-costs and what projects recover
One row for each staff member with salary, employer on-costs, bonus and the share of time charged to projects; yearly cost, cost per hour, recovered cost and overhead part fill in.
Vehicle fleet running costs and cost per km
One row for each vehicle with its monthly distance and costs; total per month, cost per km, cost per year, the driver phone and a status that flags a high cost per km fill in.
One row for each policy with insurer, cover, premium and renewal date; days left, premium per month, rate and a status that warns before a renewal fill in.
One row for each tax payment, return or licence with due date, amount and the date you paid; days left and a status that warns before a deadline fill in.
Bank loans, leases and credit facilities
One row for each loan or lease with amount, rate, term and start; monthly payment, payments made, balance, end date, interest over the life and a status fill in.
One row for each machine or asset with cost, purchase date, life and residual value; depreciation per year and month, accumulated depreciation, book value and a status fill in.
One row for each payment to an owner with the tax withheld; net amount, the owner total for the year to date and a flag for large draws fill in.
One row for each manager and quarter with the revenue and margin target; actual revenue and margin from Revenue by Month, the share achieved and a status fill in.

Ask the insurer for renewal terms
Hello, our policy "{policy}" ends on {renew}. Please send the renewal terms and the premium this week.
Hello, our work has grown since the last renewal of "{policy}". Can we review the sum insured of {sum_ins} before {renew}?
Hello, we are paying the premium of {premium} for "{policy}". Please confirm when you receive it and send the certificate.
Hello, the policy "{policy}" ended on {renew}. We need cover in force today. Please call us.
Hello, we are sending the figures for "{item}", due on {due}. Please confirm the amount of {amount} before we pay.
Ask the adviser about a deadline
Hello, "{item}" is due on {due}. Is everything ready to file and pay?
Ask for help with a late payment
Hello, "{item}" was due on {due} and is not paid. What penalty do we face and how do we fix it today?
Ask a lender for a better rate
Hello, our facility "{facility}" runs at {rate}. Can we review the rate before {review}?
Hello, please send a statement of the balance and the payments for "{facility}". Our records show {balance} left.
Hello, we may repay "{facility}" early. Please tell us the payoff figure and any fee.
Invite a staff member to a pay review
Hello {name}, we would like to meet you to review your pay and your goals. Which day this week suits you?
Hello {name}, thank you for your work this quarter. We value what you do as {role}.
Tell a staff member about a bonus
Hello {name}, your bonus for this year will be paid with the next salary. Please contact the office if you have a question.
Ask a driver for the vehicle costs
Hello {driver}, please send the odometer reading and the fuel receipts for {vehicle} this week.
Ask a driver about a high cost per km
Hello {driver}, {vehicle} costs {per_km} for each km. Can you tell us about repairs or unneeded trips?
Confirm a payment to an owner
Hello {owner}, we paid {amount} on {date}. The net amount after tax is {net}.
Hello {owner}, a payment of {amount} needs a second approval. Please reply to confirm.
Ask a client about a decision
Hello, we are waiting for your decision on "{project}". Is there news or a question about our price of {value}?
Plan the start after an award
Hello, to plan our team for "{project}" can you confirm the start date of {start}?
Offer a meeting on a proposal
Hello, we would like to present our proposal for "{project}". When can we meet?
Hello, the next payment for "{name}" is due. Our records show {revenue} of work done. Please confirm the date of payment.
Ask a client to release retention
Hello, we hold {retention} of retention on "{name}" under the contract. Please tell us when it will be released.
Hello, "{name}" is {done} complete. We will send the next progress report this week.
Hello {manager}, your revenue target for the quarter from {start} is {rev_target}. Let us meet to agree it.
Hello {manager}, you have reached {achieved} of your revenue target. Can we talk about the rest of the quarter?
Ask a client for the start date
Hello, "{name}" has not started. Please confirm the date we can begin on site.
Hello, "{name}" is past its completion date of {finish} and {remaining} of work remains. We will send a catch-up plan today.
Hello, "{name}" is nearly complete with {remaining} of work left. Please book the final inspection with us.
Request to renew an insurance policy

The policy with a sum insured of {col:insurance.sum_ins} and a yearly premium of {col:insurance.premium} ends on {col:insurance.renew}. Please send the renewal terms and the premium so that the cover continues without a gap.
Our work, our equipment and our contracts have changed since the last renewal. Please call us to review the sum insured before the renewal date.
Request for a facility review with the lender
The facility runs at {col:loans.rate} with a payment of {col:loans.pmt} each month. The balance now is {col:loans.balance} and the next review is on {col:loans.review}.
We ask for a meeting to review the rate and the term, and we will bring our latest accounts and our order book.
Instruction to the adviser for a tax or licence payment
Please prepare and file this item for the amount of {col:tax.amount}, due on {col:tax.due}. Send us the figures for approval at least five working days before the due date.
If the amount or the date is wrong, tell us now so that we avoid a penalty.
Voucher for a payment to an owner
Paid to {col:draws.owner}. Kind of payment: {col:draws.kind}. Date: {col:draws.date}.
Amount: {col:draws.amount}. Tax withheld: {col:draws.withheld}. Net paid: {col:draws.net}. Total paid to this owner this year: {col:draws.ytd}.
The payment was approved by a second owner when it was above the approval limit.
Memo on the budget for a month
Actual revenue was {col:budget.act_revenue} and actual operating profit was {col:budget.act_profit}. The profit variance is {col:budget.profit_var} and the status is {col:budget.state}.
Please explain every variance above five percent and tell us what you will do in the next month.
Cover letter for the monthly management report
Operating profit was {col:pnl.op} and net profit after tax was {col:pnl.net}, a net margin of {col:pnl.nm}. The result is {col:pnl.state} against our net margin aim.
The report goes to the owners and to the lender when the facility asks for it.
Approval to sell or scrap an asset
The book value is {col:assets.book} after accumulated depreciation of {col:assets.acc}. We ask for approval to sell or scrap this asset and to record any gain or loss against its book value.
The site manager confirms that the asset is not needed on any project.
Letter to a staff member about their pay review

Your salary is {col:staffcost.salary} each month. With on-costs and bonus the yearly cost to the company is {col:staffcost.annual}. We would like to meet you to talk about your pay, your role and your goals for next year.
Please bring any information about your work that you want us to consider.
Memo on a project that is over or under billed

The project has earned {col:wip.earned} and billed {col:wip.billed}. The difference is {col:wip.diff} and the status is {col:wip.state}. The forecast margin is {col:wip.fcst_margin} against {col:wip.plan_margin} at tender.
Please bring the billing and the cost forecast into line before the next month end.
Letter setting a quarterly target for a manager

Your revenue target for this quarter is {col:targets.rev_target} with a margin of at least {col:targets.margin_target}. So far you have reached {col:targets.achieved} of the revenue target at a margin of {col:targets.margin}.
We will review the figures with you at the end of the quarter.

Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: tax rate, margin aims, overhead aim, billing tolerance, warning days, minimum current ratio and the order book you want in months.
Fill Projects once: client, manager, contract value, dates and retention. Revenue to date, cost to date and retention held fill in from Revenue by Month.
Each month add one row on Revenue by Month for every project you built: the revenue earned and the direct cost. Profit and Loss, Profit Ranking and Business Targets fill from it.
Update WIP Report with the estimated total cost and what you billed. The share complete, the revenue earned and the over or under billing fill in, with a status.
Enter overheads on Overheads by month and group, with the budget. Staff Costs, Vehicle Fleet and Insurance Policies hold the details behind salaries, vehicles and insurance.
Record loans on Loans and Facilities, equipment on Asset Register, and every tax return and licence on Tax and Licences with its due date.
Keep Tender Pipeline up to date with the chance of each opportunity. Order Book and Backlog by Month show the secured work and the months of work left.
Add cash, receivables, stock, payables and debt on Key Ratios each month to see the current ratio, days sales outstanding and rolling margins.
Set the budget for each month on Annual Budget and the quarterly targets on Business Targets, then read the variances.
Log payments to owners on Owner Draws; large ones are flagged for a second approval.

Use the 14 calculators for overhead rate, break-even, billing, order book months, cash conversion, margins, depreciation, loan payments, bonding capacity, growth, price rises, profit per person, debt cover and cash runway.
Read Company Finance Dashboard and Charts every month before you meet the owners or the lender.
